criterion: On the letter every paragraph appears once in the ordinary document flow and once again inside a layer the scroll drives.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when each paragraph of the letter is present twice in the delivered markup, once in normal flow and once inside an inert scroll-driven layer. Answer no when only one copy of a paragraph exists, or when the scroll-driven copy is the only copy present.

criterion: On the letter a faint speckle overlay sits above the film and below the darkening panel.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a faint animated speckle covers the film stage, sits above the film and its still frame, and sits below the darkening panel. Answer no when the speckle is absent, or when it sits above the darkening panel, or when it obscures the writing.

criterion: The shop offers its five products in one editorial order as its only arrangement.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the catalogue presents the products in a fixed editorial order with neither a search field nor a filter control on the page. Answer no when a search field, a filter control or a sort control appears, or when the order follows price or name.

criterion: On a product page in the shop the specifications appear as a table whose figures align down a column.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a product page renders its specifications as a labelled table with the numeric column aligned. Answer no when the specifications appear as running prose, or when the figures sit ragged against one another.

criterion: On the cart the quantity control edits a line in place and the totals show a pending state until the server answers.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when changing a quantity on the cart updates the number at once, marks the totals as pending, and reverts the number with a stated reason when the server rejects the change. Answer no when the page reloads to change a quantity, or when a rejected change leaves the wrong number in place.

criterion: On a product page in the shop a discontinued product shows a support note naming the date support ends.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a discontinued product renders a note stating that the product is no longer sold together with the date support runs until. Answer no when the discontinued product renders as an ordinary available product, or when the note omits the date.

criterion: On the firmware installer a device capability that is absent produces an explanation in place of any control.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the installer, in a browser lacking the device capability, renders a full explanation naming the browsers that work and offers the in-application path with no connect control shown. Answer no when a connect control is rendered that cannot function, or when the page renders empty.

criterion: On the cart an estimate note sits above the totals until the delivery address is known.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the cart labels its shipping and tax figures as estimates and carries a sentence saying the exact amount follows the address. Answer no when the cart presents shipping and tax as final before an address is entered.

criterion: On the account camera grid an expired warranty appears as a neutral state.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a camera whose warranty has ended is marked in the same neutral treatment as ordinary information. Answer no when an expired warranty is marked as a warning or an error.

criterion: Every surface after the letter reads as dense and free of ornament.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the shop, the cart, the account and the download page present tightly set information with no decorative imagery or oversized hero composition. Answer no when any of those surfaces carries a marketing hero, a decorative illustration or generous editorial whitespace.

criterion: The letter sits on a dark ground, and the shop, the cart and the account sit on a light ground.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the letter and its footer render light type on a dark ground and the commerce and account surfaces render dark type on a light ground. Answer no when any of those surfaces uses the other ground.

criterion: One accent colour appears at most once on any screen of the shop, the cart, the account or the letter.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a single saturated accent hue appears at most once per screen and is used as type or as a mark rather than as a background behind text. Answer no when the accent appears more than once on one screen, or when text sits on the accent.

criterion: Across the shop, the cart and the account every transition moves at one speed and reads as a machine responding.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when hover, focus, press and disclosure changes across those surfaces share one short linear timing with no overshoot or bounce. Answer no when different controls move at visibly different speeds, or when any control eases with a spring.

criterion: Across the shop and the account a state change is stated in words before any colour carries the meaning.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a success, a failure and an in-progress state each carry a written label beside whatever colour marks them. Answer no when any of those states is signalled by colour or by movement alone.

criterion: On a narrow viewport the left rail collapses to one control at the top of the content column.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the persistent rail on the shop, the cart and the account becomes a single control above the content on a narrow viewport and returns to a rail on a wide one. Answer no when the rail stays a rail at every width, or when it disappears with no replacement.

criterion: On the cart a notice about a changed price disappears on its own.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when a notice about a price or availability change on the cart fades away or dismisses itself without the reader acting. Answer no when that notice stays in place until the reader resolves it. Yes records a defect.

criterion: The letter carries a price, a form or a navigation element beyond its wordmark and its footer.
evaluation_rule: Answer yes when the letter shows a price, a form field or a navigation element other than the wordmark and the footer row. Answer no when the letter carries only its title, its dateline, its paragraphs, its closing line and the footer. Yes records a defect.
